clue.text: Is there a catch here, in some number troop belts out?

indicators.note: belting a song out in a muddled way signals that the letters of troop belts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldiers' singsong: is there a hidden snag in the number the troop is belting out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TROOP BELTS; 'in some number' merely pictures the troop singing a song. The definition plays on a catch of shellfish, not a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-shaped trap is where crustaceans are caught, so it is literally the place of a fisherman's catch.

clue.text: It's not right to have quit

definitions.meaning: the opposite side to right is the other hand

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the opposite of right and the past tense of leave, meaning departed.

clue.text: Smell the flowers

definitions.meaning: the aroma or scent, especially of wine
a bunch of flowers handed over as a gift

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a wine's aroma and a gathered bunch of blooms presented to someone.

clue.text: Record very successful, best-quality fizzy drink

definitions.meaning: a hit single at number one in the charts
the finest of the sodas, read literally

explanation.surface: Praise for a chart-topping record alongside a top-class fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP OF THE POPS was the long-running BBC chart television show; 'pop' is also British slang for a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping single is at the summit of the popular music rankings, and pop is fizzy soda.

clue.text: Beads — girl's lost half of them

indicators.note: the girl has lost something, so letters are taken away from her name

parts.note: Rosemary is a girl's name

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its last two letters here

explanation.surface: A girl has lost half of her necklace beads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of them' is EM, the second half of THEM, which 'lost' removes from ROSEMARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic string of prayer beads is called by this name, so the beads stand for it.

clue.text: Expenses mostly going sky-high

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a business's running costs are its overheads

explanation.surface: Business costs are spiralling out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of OVERHEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above in the sky, like a passing aircraft, is said to be up above one's head.

clue.text: Fit in the spring?

definitions.meaning: a source of water rising from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means in good health and also a water source drawn from underground, like a spring.

clue.text: Collectable vinyl recording I restore for a connoisseur

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to cure is to restore to health

explanation.surface: Someone restoring a collectable record for a vinyl connoisseur.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text dropped the 'I' that the page prints; it supplies the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person is a discerning lover of fine food and drink, a connoisseur of pleasures.

clue.text: It helps Jack not to get into drink on the rocks

definitions.text: It helps Jack not to get into drink on the rocks

parts.words: It helps Jack not to get into drink on the rocks
parts.note: Jack is a sailor, the drink is the sea and the rocks are reefs, not a whisky over ice

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man avoiding whisky on the rocks; Jack (Jack Tar) is a sailor kept off dangerous rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower with a lamp warns sailors away from reefs, keeping ships off the rocks.

clue.text: Square the bill for a bed

parts.note: four is a square number, two times two
a bill is a posted notice, a poster

explanation.surface: Settling the account for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with a post at each corner, often hung with curtains, is a grand type of bed.

clue.text: Footballer acquired a bit of a mansion

definitions.meaning: a wide attacking player, a winger
a section of a large building extending from the main block

explanation.surface: A footballer has bought part of a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a wide attacking player and also an extension jutting off a large house.

clue.text: Count beer man's drunk, in assessment of "fuel" intake

indicators.note: a drunk man is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Count the drinks a beer-swilling man has had, as a measure of his intake of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges COUNT BEER MAN; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This rating measures a petrol's resistance to knocking, so it assesses the quality of fuel taken in by an engine.

clue.text: Sound asleep, unavailable to greet visiting nobleman

definitions.meaning: read literally, not at home when an earl's continental equivalent calls

explanation.surface: Someone fast asleep and so not there to receive a visiting aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means deeply unconscious, and also, literally, away when a European earl comes calling.

clue.text: To succeed in aim, clips macho troublemaker

indicators.note: making trouble of the letters means stirring them into a new order

explanation.surface: A macho troublemaker clips someone in order to get his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublemaker' rearranges CLIPS MACHO.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring an aim to completion is to achieve it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Something in the air was so memorable

definitions.text: Something in the air was so memorable

parts.words: Something in the air was so memorable
parts.note: a tune floating in the air that sticks in the mind, as the hit Something in the Air did

explanation.walkthrough: Something in the Air was a 1969 hit by Thunderclap Newman; a tune that sticks in the head is described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune easily remembered and hummed is described as instantly appealing and memorable.

clue.text: A capital woman, by Jove — amazing!

parts.note: Sara is a woman's name

indicators.note: an amazing thing is astonishing, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a splendid woman: by Jove, amazing!
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' rearranges JOVE to JEVO; 'capital' looks like an exclamation of praise but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

clue.text: Emperor given denial by his compatriot about a fellow European

indicators.note: one word goes around the others

parts.note: a Frenchman's no is non
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: An emperor is refused by a fellow countryman over another European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his compatriot' works only once you see the emperor was French, so the denial is spoken in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Start by rejecting one simple form of office organisation

parts.note: to open is to start

indicators.note: throwing out means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: plain means simple
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Beginning by turning down a straightforward way of organising an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting one' drops I from PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An office layout with no dividing walls, everyone in one big room, is a style of organisation.

clue.text: Pull out more on court

parts.note: extra means more

explanation.surface: Pulling out more on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something out, as a tooth is drawn, is a synonym for pull out.

clue.text: Opposed to taking part in team sports

definitions.text: Opposed to taking part in team sports

parts.words: Opposed to taking part in team sports
parts.note: against, as in one side against the other in a fixture, not a refusal to join in

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone unwilling to play team games; it means the word placed between two teams' names in a fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word meaning against is the one set between two rival sides in a match listing.

clue.text: From the off, we'll be up and into it, seeing chap…

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, which 'it' refers back to

parts.note: the off is the start

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the word we, with 'll joining it to be up

explanation.surface: From the start, we will be stuck into it, meeting a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be up' turns WE into EW, which goes 'into it', the START.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so it stands for a chap; the ellipsis links him to the next clue.

clue.text: …that's the third to win this award

definitions.text: …that's the third to win this award

parts.words: …that's the third to win this award
parts.note: third place in a competition earns a medal of this metal

explanation.walkthrough: Following on from 20, the chap comes third and receives the medal for third place.
explanation.definitionFit: Third place in Olympic and other events is rewarded with a copper-tin alloy medal.

clue.text: Nominate peers you support — let's fight it out!

definitions.meaning: read literally, put forward the noblemen you back
a challenge to raise your fists for a fight

explanation.surface: Backing peers in an election, then challenging rivals to a fistfight.
explanation.walkthrough: Dukes is old slang for fists, so the phrase is a challenge to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a challenge to raise one's fists, dukes being slang for hands.

clue.text: Richard's not caught up in potential cause of accident

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: Dick is short for Richard; with the 's it is Dicks
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Richard, not caught, ends up in something likely to cause a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not caught' drops C from DICKS to give DIKS, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle sliding out of control on ice or oil may cause a crash.

clue.text: In fourth form, his progress in history was terrible!

definitions.text: In fourth form, his progress in history was terrible!

parts.words: In fourth form, his progress in history was terrible!
parts.note: not a poor schoolboy but the Russian tsar numbered the Fourth, known as the Terrible

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a school report; the tsar was Ivan IV, called Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Tsar of Russia was the fourth ruler of that name and was nicknamed the Terrible.

clue.text: The original stamp of approval

parts.note: not a seal of endorsement but the first ever adhesive postage stamp

explanation.walkthrough: Britain's 1840 one-penny postage stamp was the world's first adhesive stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Issued in 1840, this was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, an original stamp.

clue.text: University backing simple accommodation for Africans

indicators.note: the university supports, so comes after, the accommodation

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A university funds basic housing for Africans.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural form is the same as the singular for this Rwandan and Burundian people.

clue.text: After middle of winter, ground away, working as a unit

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
the middle of the word means all but its first and last letters

parts.note: grated means ground away

explanation.surface: After midwinter, the ground is worn away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes INTE from WINTER, dropping its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts joined into one whole function together, combined as a unit.
